title: Compute brief - 25 November 2026
description: Orders up, stocks down: Dell booked $60.2 billion of AI orders and a record $132.3 billion backlog while chip stocks gave back the Huang rally, and grids from Estonia to Finland and France became the binding constraint. Wire: Dell AI backlog, XTX Kajaani, Estonia 3.3 GW requests, Google Indre 1.2 GW connection, US Army power-plus-data-centre RFP, Samsung HBM base die crunch, South Africa power station sites. Tape: 70 confirms, 0 ticks, 0 NEW.
og_kicker: Backlog at a record, chips in a selloff.
lede: The order book and the stock market split. Dell booked $60.2 billion of AI server orders in its third quarter and ended with a record $132.3 billion AI backlog, lifting full-year revenue guidance to $202 billion, yet the Philadelphia semiconductor index fell 7.9 per cent on 24 November and chip stocks kept falling on 25 November as AI financing and rate worries returned. Power, not demand, is the constraint in Europe: Estonia's grid operator has 3.3 GW of data centre requests, nearly twice national peak, XTX opened 22.5 MW in Kajaani while warning that grid permits now take years, and a Google unit sought a 1.2 GW connection in France that RTE says would take seven to eight years. In silicon, Samsung is reported short of HBM base die capacity, with demand seen doubling to about 30,000 wafers a month in 2027. List prices held for a thirteenth straight trading day: 70 confirms, 0 ticks, 0 NEW, with Lambda H100 at $4.59 and B200 at $7.69 ahead of Crusoe's posted 1 December step-up.
